###chapter 2 The Kiss Mark on Her Neck

###chapter 3 His Odd Behavior

Every colleague in the office acted extremely calm, but it was this nothing happened attitude that was the most dangerous. Layla could feel the countless ambiguous, curious, mysterious, and knowing glances whenever she turned her back. Although different from the previous hostile looks, it was still troubling.

Even when Layla went to the restroom, she could hear them gossiping intensely behind her back.

Everyone quickly gossiped.

###chapter 412 Thinking About Another Man?

The question hung in the air for a few seconds of silence.

Then...

"Of course, it counts! If you have a boyfriend and you're still flirting with other men, that's already betrayal. Now, she was getting caught doing that in the office. If that's not betrayal, what is?" Female Colleague A exclaimed, gripping her lipstick tightly.

Wasn't it said that people's interest in news only lasted a week?

Still, deceiving herself was better than doing nothing.

###chapter 413 He's the One Truly Disturbed

###chapter 414 No Messages

###chapter 415 A Necessary Resolution

The CEO's office was also shrouded in a tense atmosphere.

Frustration.

"Mr. Evans... aren't you leaving?" The secretary poked her head in.

The sunlight outside was just right.

The pillow beside her was empty.

Laughter came from downstairs.

Susan felt so at peace.

Waking up to see the sunlight and hear her husband and kids' happy laughter made her life feel perfect, her heart full of joy.

Her hand rested on her high, rounded belly. "Good morning, baby."

She got up to freshen up.

Even though her face was a bit puffy from pregnancy, she looked radiant, her eyes bright and full of life, her lips rosy, and her skin smooth and flawless like a pearl.

Susan smiled at herself in the mirror.

"It looks great, both of you did a wonderful job," Susan said with a smile, her round face looking especially kind. "My two little darlings are amazing."

She bent down and kissed their adorable little faces.

"I'm amazing too," Caleb said, leaning in for a kiss.

"Alright, you're amazing too," Susan said, used to his childishness, often competing with the kids for attention. She gave him a kiss, amused.

Caleb was delighted.

"Keep going, tonight is Christmas Eve, and we still have to open presents," Susan said, sitting on the couch to watch.

"Did you hear that? Keep going, I'll stay with your mom."

The two little ones eagerly continued.

Susan teased, "You're just looking for an excuse to be lazy."

"How can you call this being lazy? Being with my wife is the most important thing," Caleb said, now like a clingy child, spending all his time at home with his wife and kids when not working, going nowhere else.

Watching Oliver and Candy happily running around, Susan couldn't help but feel sentimental, "Do you remember how we spent Christmas last year?"

"Yes. It snowed that day, Oliver had just had surgery, and we spent it in the hospital with him."

"Yes, it was tough back then," Susan said, shaking her head.

Caleb hugged her soft, fragrant body. Pregnant women seemed to have a particularly pleasant scent, "Yes, but it's all in the past. Now, we're reaping the rewards. We're adding a new addition to the family next Christmas, and things are going to be much more lively."

"Yes," Susan imagined the scene. She used to think one child was enough, but now she loved the idea of a bustling household. Three kids, yes, that would be perfect.

In the future, when they grow up a bit, they could travel the world as a family of five.

That day would come soon.

By noon, it started snowing, and the snow got heavier. When Susan woke up from a nap, the yard was already covered in a thick layer of snow.

"Mommy, wake up for a snowball fight," Oliver burst into the room excitedly.

Candy, like a little tail, tagged along Oliver, bouncing and jumping with excitement, "Mommy! Mommy!"

###chapter 599: The Greatest Joy in Life

Susan peered out the window. The snow had finally stopped, leaving a thick blanket on the ground. It'd be a total waste not to have a snowball fight with all that snow. Plus, kids love playing in the snow, and she was all for it.

This was the most gratifying and fulfilling moment of Susan's life.

From this moment on, she could let go of all her burdens and worries.

How lucky she was to have a husband who loved and cherished her, a sensible son, a sweet and adorable daughter, and an unborn baby.

To be loved, to have something to do, and to have something to look forward to-this is the greatest happiness in life.

She believed that in the coming years and decades, their family would have reunions. Every Christmas, they would gather together, even when she and Caleb were old and surrounded by grandchildren, enjoying the happiness of family.

###chapter 600: A Family of Six

Three years later.

New Year's Day.

A Rolls-Royce pulled up at the Hilton Hotel.

First out was this tall, good-looking dude with a red scarf, making everyone go "wow."

Then, this seven or eight-year-old kid with thick brows and big eyes, just as handsome and cute, hopped out. He was like a mini-me of the guy.

The tall guy scooped up the little one and grabbed his wife's hand. The handsome boy held the curly-haired girl's hand.

Three years into their marriage, and they were still as sweet as when they were dating, loving each other more every day.

The most beautiful love in the world is holding hands and growing old together.

###chapter 608 Swallowing the Grievance

###chapter 609: Three Days and Nights of Torment

Every time she was about to doze off, they'd wake her up. They were basically saying, "Sign this, or you ain't sleeping," trying to break her down.

Staying awake was pure torture. Layla couldn't help but think, "People must've died from this no-sleep crap." She almost gave in a few times, but some tiny bit of sanity kept her hanging on. She bit her lips till they bled, just to stay awake.

###chapter 617: Ten Months of Pregnancy

"Can't people sleep?"

"Keep it up, and I'll call the police!"

###chapter 725 A Clean Break

It really hurt.

Juniper thought, 'It's all my fault. I'm a sinner. Staying here will only continue to harm myself and others. Harden your heart, Juniper. Leave this city. Escape as far as you can, and stop hurting others and yourself. Just think of it as a dream. One day it will all be over.'

In the morning.

They were truly lenient with themselves but strict with others.

###chapter 727 Leaving in Three Days

Bennie interrupted her, "Don't give me that crap! Where's the money?"

"I really don't have any left, not a penny."

"I'm telling you, you'd better give me the money. Don't push me, or I'll drag you down with me!"

Mira regretted not killing him that night when he was drunk and asleep. She should have done it. If he didn't die, she would die at his hands.

###chapter 729 Discovering the Truth

###chapter 739 Missing Each Other

A flood of emotions washed over her.

Shaking her head, she told herself, "It's all in the past."

The next morning, at Harmony City Airport.

People coming and going.

A striking figure walked out of the gate.

That face, gentle and noble, wearing a simple white shirt, exuding an air of elegance. 

From head to toe, there were no conspicuous luxury items, yet he looked undeniably distinguished.

Almost as soon as he exited the gate, his phone rang.

"Off the plane?" a woman's gentle voice came through.

She knew his landing time.

Anthony didn't like this feeling of being closely watched.

Maybe it was concern, but this precise timing inevitably felt like a constraint.

Another face flashed before Anthony's eyes.

She would look beautiful in a wedding dress, right?

But he immediately banished her from his mind. 

Whether he loved her or not, his bride was Hera, and that was an unchangeable fact. 

From body to heart, he had to remain loyal.

In August, the scorching sun of Libertonia was blazing. 

As soon as he left the airport, a heatwave hit, everything was white and blinding, making people dizzy.

Anthony's vision went black.

In that instant, that face was particularly clear.

He didn't know why, but in a foreign land, he remembered her more clearly.

He didn't even know where she was, didn't dare to inquire about her, fearing that his already unsettled heart would be stirred again.

Juniper?

His heart raced.

Maybe he was mistaken.

This was just another of his countless illusions.

There's a saying that goes, after falling in love with her, everyone you meet looks like her.

He just saw a resemblance, it wasn't her.

They couldn't meet in their own country, how could they meet thousands of miles away?

He smiled bitterly. He felt like he was under a spell, almost losing his mind.

Juniper... Juniper... 

This name echoed in his dreams countless times, the reason he couldn't sleep well.

But what he didn't know was, that really was his dream-haunting Juniper.

Rarely not having to work late, Juniper felt particularly quiet and aimless in her small apartment.

Not wanting to be alone, she went out for a walk, to see the night view.

Unexpectedly, just a street away, was him.

Standing by the river, feeling the breeze, the night wind had a gentle scent.

Another man tried to hit on her, a tall, handsome Virtalia man, but Juniper waved him off, saying she was already married.

Two days later.

At the company, 8:50 AM.

Jack was in a formal suit today, looking particularly sharp and handsome.

Everyone else in the company wore formal attire to work, except Jack.

The top-floor elevator opened.

###chapter 740 A Definitive End

The man in a sharp suit walked out of the elevator.

Juniper looked up with a smile, and in an instant...

She was struck as if by lightning, completely stunned.

Her body trembled violently. 'Anthony? Why is it him?'

The emotions she had painstakingly calmed over the past three months surged again, like a stormy sea.

In the moment their eyes met, Anthony was also stunned, his blood running cold.

Clearly, this unexpected reunion caught both of them off guard.

Time seemed to stand still, and the air was sucked dry.

Juniper could only hear her own chaotic heartbeat.

Thump, thump, thump-it was racing.

However, the reunion of adults is often like this: no matter how turbulent their hearts are, they hide it well.

Her lips turned a bit pale, and she pretended to be calm, avoiding his gaze.

The moment she looked away, Anthony understood her intention.

She was pretending not to know him.

"I was wondering who created such a legend in the industry in just a few months. Turns out it's Mr. Eilish. Long time no see," Jack, who had dealt with him before, stepped forward enthusiastically to shake hands.

She had come to Libertonia and become the secretary to the general manager of this big company.

In other words, did she come to Libertonia to avoid him?

Anthony's mood was far from calm, with many thoughts swirling in his mind.

Juniper followed them with her head down.

In Jack's office, there was a tea set. "Mr. Eilish, do you like tea? I have some top-quality tea here that you can't even get back home. You must try it. Juniper, make some tea."

His possessiveness towards her was really strong, even now.

If he brought up the past or showed too much concern, it would only make her more like a frightened bird, more eager to avoid him.

The ring on his ring finger was low-key but glaring.

The most self-destructive thing is to make no progress and keep repeating the same mistakes. It's been three months; she couldn't have made no changes at all.

Juniper's mood shifted from the initial turmoil and nervousness to calmness and disillusionment.

No matter how good he was, he was now someone else's husband.

It turns out that completely giving up is such a short process.

###chapter 742 A New Romance
